title: game-design-system
universal_lens: The game creation system is a constrained, sequential dynamical system. It enforces a strict topological ordering of phases (Plan → Build), where state transitions are gated by logical predicates. The invariant 'one pipeline, one speed' ensures deterministic execution bounds, while the asset manifest acts as a minimal sufficient statistic for the design space.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the mandatory plan phase (§§1–5) functions as a Bayesian prior construction over the latent game state space. The `assets.csv` serves as the conformal calibration set, explicitly enumerating observable features before inference. Blocking points act as high-confidence thresholds; if the posterior uncertainty on the STYLE FORMULA exceeds tolerance, the pipeline halts to query the user.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, the 'no code before PLAN closes' rule maps to a hard state-transition constraint in a finite state machine. Parallelization of independent asset jobs represents concurrent evaluation of disjoint subgraphs, while sequential dependencies enforce causal ordering. The iterative loop ensures that every micro-state transition is validated against the global gate predicate before committing.

primitives.name: Phase-Ordered State Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: The phases themselves never interleave — no game code before PLAN closes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: Phase index (dimensionless integer); t: temporal execution step (ms)
primitives.assumptions: Phases form a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with strict topological sort constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Occurs when speculative execution bypasses the planning DAG, leading to architectural debt and unbounded state complexity.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's rigid pre-computation vs. runtime execution boundaries. Ensures no runtime logic is instantiated without a fully resolved static analysis layer.
layer2.telemetry: Zero lines of executable game logic committed prior to the closure timestamp of the final planning section.

primitives.name: Asset Manifest Projection
primitives.verbatim_quote: > - **Asset manifest — the only written planning artifact, mandatory always**: planning emits `design/assets.csv` (in the game project under `design/` — it ships with the game) listing every visual/audio asset the build needs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: A: Set of all required assets; M: Manifest matrix (rows = |A|, cols = attributes)
primitives.assumptions: The design space can be fully projected onto a finite, enumerable set of discrete resource requirements.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the game relies on infinite procedural generation without bounded seed parameters, making explicit enumeration impossible.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the GSI feature extraction layer. The manifest is the explicit basis vector set for the subsequent generative subspace, preventing dimensionality explosion during the build phase.
layer2.telemetry: 100% coverage of referenced media IDs in the final build binary matched against rows in `assets.csv`.

primitives.name: Uniform Execution Floor
primitives.verbatim_quote: > - **One pipeline, one speed — and it is the floor.** Every request runs the same lean pipeline; there are no heavier or lighter modes.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: v: Pipeline velocity (constant); R: Request complexity (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Computational cost is decoupled from semantic simplicity; the overhead of rigorous planning is strictly positive and constant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violated by heuristic shortcuts (e.g., 'it's just a simple game'), introducing variance and increasing the probability of edge-case failures.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSE's fixed-timestep simulation law. By enforcing a constant processing depth regardless of input magnitude, the system guarantees bounded worst-case latency and prevents mode-switching bugs.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of pipeline duration across requests of vastly different scopes approaches zero after normalizing for asset generation time.

We can model this as a state machine $S = (Q, \Sigma, \delta, q_0, F)$, where $Q$ represents the distinct phases (Profile, Laws, Concept, etc.). The transition function $\delta$ is heavily constrained: it is not merely a function of the current state and input, but requires the satisfaction of a complex boolean predicate $G(state)$—the 'gate'. For instance, the transition from Design to Implementation is blocked until $assets.csv$ exists and the STYLE FORMULA is derived. This enforces a causal dependency graph where downstream states cannot be populated without upstream sufficient statistics. The 'One pipeline, one speed' primitive introduces an invariant metric tensor over the state space; the 'distance' or computational effort required to traverse from $q_{start}$ to $q_{end}$ is constant, independent of the semantic weight of the request. This prevents the common optimization failure where simple tasks bypass critical validation steps, thereby maintaining structural integrity. The parallelization rule ('parallelize what is genuinely independent') is a direct application of graph theory to the task DAG, maximizing throughput without violating causal edges. The breakdown regime occurs when the agent attempts to shortcut the DAG (e.g., writing code before the plan closes), which mathematically equates to introducing cycles or backward edges in a strictly acyclic process, inevitably leading to undefined behavior and technical debt.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This system traces its lineage to the Waterfall model's strict phase gating, but modernized through Agile's iterative feedback loops and Lean manufacturing's waste reduction. Mathematically, it echoes the axiomatic method in geometry: definitions and postulates (Plan) must be fully established before any theorems (Code) can be proven. It also mirrors compiler design, where lexical analysis and parsing (Planning) must complete and produce an Abstract Syntax Tree (Asset Manifest) before code generation (Implementation) can commence.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The system models the 'user' not as a passive recipient but as a stochastic actor whose inputs may be hostile, ambiguous, or incomplete. The 'blocking points' (e.g., STYLE FORMULA approval) are essentially Bayesian updates where the system's internal confidence interval drops below a threshold, necessitating an external oracle (the user) to resolve the ambiguity. It assumes the user's mental model of the game is initially latent and must be explicitly parameterized through the 'Experience Formula' before the system can reliably simulate it.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists between the 'Concept' layer and the 'Code' layer. If the 'Four Pillars' (mechanics, story, aesthetics, technology) are not mutually reinforcing—if one pillar serves no other—the system must halt. This is an anti-collinearity check: ensuring that the vectors representing each pillar are linearly independent yet span the desired experience space. Leakage occurs if implementation details (e.g., a specific rendering library) bleed into the high-level concept, violating the abstraction barrier and causing the 'architecture = minimizing cost of change' law to fail.
